prompt: Validate a command line -- argument count, a numeric repeat count, and its allowed range -- printing one specific error line per problem, then repeat the joined words.

explanation: Validation reads best as a series of guards: each check prints its message and returns, so by the time the real work starts every assumption holds. The order is not arbitrary -- args.length must be checked before args[0] is read, and args[0] must parse before its value can be range checked. Integer.parseInt signals a bad number by throwing NumberFormatException rather than returning a flag value, so that check needs a try/catch instead of an if.
hints: Declare int count; outside the try and assign it inside, so it is still in scope for the range checks afterwards.
Catch NumberFormatException specifically; print the message including args[0] and return from the catch block.
Build the joined line once (a StringBuilder, or String.join(" ", java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(args, 1, args.length))) and then print that same line count times.
